results.summary: This project implements a set of basic logic gates (AND, OR, NAND) on a Tiny Tapeout tile. It is built in Wokwi and takes eight input pins, producing outputs that reflect the gate operations. The documentation is minimal, consisting only of placeholder text, so the exact mapping of inputs to outputs is not fully described. It appears to be an educational or test design, but the lack of detail limits its usefulness.

This design is a 4-bit binary counter that uses T flip-flops to divide the input clock frequency. The divided clock then drives four D flip-flops to produce the counter outputs. It is implemented in Wokwi and requires an external clock signal to operate. The documentation is brief and does not specify external hardware or detailed testing steps.

This project combines AND, inverter, and XNOR gates to produce eight outputs based on eight button inputs. It is designed in Wokwi and intended for interactive testing by pressing buttons and observing the outputs. The documentation is sparse, with only a brief description of the gate connections and testing procedure. No external hardware is mentioned.

This design implements AND, NAND, and OR gates that take two inputs and produce three outputs. Additionally, it includes a clock divider using 16 flip-flops, with outputs taken at the 12th and 16th stages. The project is built in Wokwi and is intended as a test or educational example. The documentation is minimal and does not describe external hardware requirements.

This project implements a Hamming (7,4) encoder and decoder with single-bit error correction. It uses eight input and output pins, with a mode selection pin to switch between encoding and decoding. In decode mode, it can correct single-bit errors and reports when a correction occurs. The design is built in Wokwi and is documented with pin descriptions and testing instructions.

This is a test design with eight input and eight output pins, but the documentation is essentially empty, containing only the words 'test' and 'test it'. The functionality is not described, and no external hardware is mentioned. It appears to be a placeholder or minimal test project. Due to the lack of information, the design's purpose cannot be determined.

This project displays the letter 'Y' on a 7-segment display when an 8-bit binary code (137 in decimal) is input. It uses eight input pins for the binary code and seven output pins to drive the segments. The design is built in Wokwi and requires an external 7-segment display connected to the outputs. The documentation explains the operation and testing procedure clearly.

This project is titled 'Tiney Tapeout Test Gates' and claims to test logic gates and a clock divider, but the documentation is filled with placeholder text ('123') and all pins are marked as 'not used'. There is no meaningful description of the design's functionality or how to test it. It appears to be an incomplete or abandoned project. Due to the lack of documentation, no further details can be provided.

This design is an 8-bit backward counter that decrements at the rate of the input clock. It outputs the count on eight pins, which can be connected to LEDs for visual feedback. The project is built in Wokwi and requires eight external LEDs to display the count. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the basic operation.

This is a simple test project that connects inputs to outputs through four logic gates, with the outputs driving a 7-segment display. Enabling specific inputs causes the display to show letters or a dot. It is built in Wokwi and requires an external 7-segment display. The documentation is minimal but provides enough information to test the basic functionality.
